text:
Recommendation: Keep the note app running on 1 person; have the other 3 test one AI agent idea for 6 weeks before deciding anything bigger.
Why:
- Shutting down trades a measured asset for an unmeasured one: even with no new sales, 2% monthly churn leaves roughly $12,500 of the current $16,000 MRR after a year.
- The claim that agents are a better opportunity is untested: no specific idea, buyer, or demand signal has been named, and investors fund traction, not hot categories. The 40 paying teams are existing traction and the cheapest pool for a pilot.
Risks and unknowns:
- Splitting effort 1 person on the app and 3 on the new idea risks drifting into half-effort on both; the 6-week gate needs to be enforced strictly.
- 3+ paid pilots or a term sheet requiring a full pivot would justify going all-in; zero customer interest in the pilot pitch would make the agent plan a no-go.
Next steps:
1. By Oct 2, check runway (cash divided by net monthly burn): 3+ months is fine; if under 3 months, sell the app as a running business instead of shutting it down.
2. By Oct 9, pitch an agent built on customers' notes to 10 of the 40 teams: success is 3+ saying they'd pay; fewer than 3 means stop.
3. By Nov 9, try to sign paid pilots: 3+ means decide the app's fate; 0 means keep the app as is.
